decisions.statement: An act here reaches the records kept beside the calling agent's page for the subagents under it.
A record taken here is appended to the edits the calling agent keeps of its own.
A record is said with the subagent that left it, the time the seat took it, and what it does.
An edit is said the way every act over the edits kept says an edit.
A record saying no subagent or no time is said as saying none rather than refused.
A record whose line reads as no edit is said as one rather than refusing the file.
The records are said in the order the seat took them rather than in the order a name sorts.
A record is numbered by its place in what the seat keeps.
An act naming paths reads each path against the repository root.
A path naming no record refuses that act rather than being passed over.
A record whose line reads as no edit is reached by no path.
An agent keeping no record is said rather than refused.
A write here takes a lock keyed on the file the write writes.
A write reads the file again inside that lock rather than trusting an earlier reading.
A file a write leaves no line in is taken away rather than left empty.
Whether a record landed already is worked out here from the body that record names.
A record fits where the text it was drafted against is there to change.
A record has left its text where the body already holds what that record leaves.
A record leaving no text behind is judged by what that record fits alone.
A record that fits and has left its text cannot be judged landed.
A record that fits and has not left its text is taken.
A record that fits nothing and has left its text reads as landed already.
A record that fits nothing and has left no text reads as stale.
A record that cannot be judged landed is taken only where the caller says so.
A record is judged against the bodies on disk with the edits this agent keeps replayed first.
The records are judged in the order the seat took them, each against what the one before leaves.
Every record a path names is taken, so a chain of records over one path is taken whole.
A refusal names each record held back and why that record was held back.
A refusal over a record that cannot be judged names the call reading that record whole.
A take that refuses leaves every record where it is and keeps no edit.
Nothing here lands a record.

definition: the acts run over the records a seat keeps for the subagents under it
